newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Diana consults clairvoyant with Al Fayed.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Diana consults clairvoyant with Al Fayed.

text.p: Princess Diana has flown by Harrods helicopter with her new love Dodi Al Fayed to consult a fortuneteller about her future.
The latest bizarre twist in the romance that has gripped Britain was revealed by a camera-toting schoolgirl who spotted the couple landing in a field for the consultation with psychic Rita Rogers.

"It's not every day you get to take a picture of a Princess. It would have been nice to have talked to her but she seemed in an awful hurry to get away," 11-year-old Emma Radford told the Evening Standard on Wednesday.

But she was not impressed with the new man in the life of one of the world's most glamorous and photographed women. "He's short, bald, fat and ugly," she said of the son of Mohamed Al Fayed, owner of the luxury Harrods store.
The villagers of Lower Pilsley in northern England were alerted to the arrival of the couple on Tuesday when Rogers' husband lit a bonfire in their back garden to guide the helicopter in.

Rogers has long been the favourite clairvoyant of Diana who is said to have consulted her after being recommended by the Duchess of York, the other royal daughter-in-law whose marriage ended in divorce.

But she is no kiss-and-tell clairvoyant. She refused to give any details to reporters and has said: "I enjoy my work but there is no way I would discuss my clients. I am very, very loyal to my clients. My job is like being a priestess."

Interest in Diana's lovelife has soared since the publication on Sunday of fuzzy paparazzi pictures that showed her embracing the 41-year-old film producer whilst on a Mediterranean cruise around Corsica and Sardinia.
Tabloid papers were awash with details of Rita Rogers' predictions, for which she charges 35 pounds ($55).
She apparently once told the Duchess of York, former wife of Prince Andrew, that she saw a vision of her as First Lady of the United States to John Kennedy Junior.
But Princess Diana did not have the tabloid photo coverage entirely to herself.
Many splashed pictures of Prince William posing with his younger brother Harry and father, Prince Charles, whilst on holiday together in Scotland.
The Sun, giving top marks to the 15-year-old who has often shunned the cameras, decided: "This is a the moment when Prince William showed a new maturity and faced up to his life as our future king."
